positions.name: AuthorityOverKestrelwoodRecord
positions.frame: Who holds authority to decide what is known, forgotten, or asserted about the Kestrelwood spectrograph and its calibration history?
positions.why: The relational directional read treats all three expressions as the same authority-ranking move: src-1 and src-2 are imperatives commanding erasure of specific knowledge (the spectrograph, its 88.4 MHz calibration, Quill Ashgrove's work), while src-3 is a flat declarative that rewrites the institutional record by asserting a historical negative ('never calibrated'). The speech acts differ — directive vs. assertive — and conviction differs (src-1/src-2 read as settled decisions demanding compliance, src-3 as a claim asserted rather than performed as operational rule), and affect differs (activated-negative urgency in the directives vs. calm-negative resignation in the assertion). Held together, the frame reads all three as one exercise of control over what the record may contain: two enact it by command, one enacts it by fiat-assertion. The tension between commanding forgetting and asserting a fact-that-never-was is preserved rather than resolved — both are ways of exercising the same authority over the Kestrelwood knowledge record.
